title: field-sprint-sync-deep-dive-2026-12-07
content:
Weekly field sync deep-dive (notes + action list)
Date: 2026-12-07
Facilitator: Maya Kapoor
Attendees: Maya, Ethan, Priya, Jonah, Samir, Erin (SE), Carlos (Customer Success)

High-level summary:
- Focus this week was on three parallel installs: AtlasPay (VPC), Meridian Health (on-prem), and Quarry Solutions (high-density edge). We ran two full-day site windows (Meridian, Quarry) and one staged cutover (AtlasPay).
- Outcomes: AtlasPay cutover completed with degraded telemetry for 90m; Meridian had a storage permission regression that caused a replay; Quarry encountered network MTU and jumbo-frame inconsistency that blocked node-to-node KV-sync.
- Escalations raised: PD-723 (AtlasPay telemetry) and PD-814 (Quarry MTU edge case).

Detailed notes by customer:
1) AtlasPay (hosted-private VPC)
   - Goal: switch from shared VPC to customer-managed VPC with transit gateway policy.
   - What happened: BGP session established successfully; health checks flapped during burst traffic leading to temporary fallback to older routing policy. Observability pipeline lost ~3% of events for 90 minutes because LogForwarder container was restarted with older config.
   - Root cause hypothesis: drift between templated IAM roles and their latest applied bootstrap config (deployment variable mismatch).
   - Immediate action taken: rolled to previous routing config; SE replayed the failed traces for evaluation.
   - Next steps: Priya to run automated IAM drift check against the bootstrap repo and add a gating check in the install-harness (due 2026-12-10).

2) Meridian Health (on-prem datacenter)
   - Goal: rack install with HA pair (2x A100 nodes) + on-prem Vault integration.
   - What happened: during storage initialization, the deployment script applied ACLs that inadvertently removed the node-local service account write permission to the NFS share. System attempted to recover and triggered a partial replay causing ~15 minutes of degraded inference for test traffic.
   - Root cause: NFS mount options + id mapping mismatch across nodes; our post-install ACL reconciliation tool did not run because of a timing race.
   - Mitigation: manual permission fix (Samir + Jonah) and forced re-run of ACL reconciler.
   - Longer-term fix: make ACL reconciler idempotent and add preflight that verifies NFS id mappings before ACL changes. Samir to prototype a reconciler fix (due 2026-12-14).

3) Quarry Solutions (edge cluster)
   - Goal: scale to 8-node cluster with mixed NIC MTU (9000 and 1500).
   - What happened: KV cache sync failed intermittently; investigation showed TCP segmentation issues between nodes with different MTU settings. This surfaced as stalled step-downs and occasional model warm-start failures.
   - Root cause: customer environment had default MTU 9000 on some top-of-rack switches, but OS interface MTU was left at 1500 on a subset of return nodes (site-level config drift).
   - Action: applied a temporary bridge to enforce MTU 1500 for the cluster overlay; opened PD-814 for tracking vendor-side fix.
   - Next steps: add MTU verification to the install preflight and create a short troubleshooting guide for customers who use jumbo frames (Jonah, due 2026-12-09).

Cross-cutting notes and operational gaps:
- Observability: our LogForwarder lacks a compact checkpointing mechanism for short restarts; when restarted with older config we lose a small tail of events. Need a light-weight durable cursor. (Owner: Ethan, spike due 2026-12-13).
- Runbook: the field runbook currently assumes homogeneous MTU across nodes. Update runbook section on network preflight + add a one-shot checker script. (Owner: Priya, doc update due 2026-12-11).
- Install harness: gating tests for IAM and NFS id mappings are missing. Add fast gating checks to avoid cutovers with drift. (Owner: Priya + Samir, plan due 2026-12-10).

Action items (owners and dates):
- Priya: add IAM drift gating to install-harness; test on staging (due 2026-12-10).
- Samir: prototype idempotent ACL reconciler for NFS (due 2026-12-14).
- Jonah: write MTU preflight checker and short customer-facing MTU guide (due 2026-12-09).
- Ethan: spike for durable LogForwarder cursor (POC + benchmark, due 2026-12-13).
- Maya + Carlos: follow up with AtlasPay security on IAM role changes and provide a summary for customer (due 2026-12-09).
- Jonah + SEs: schedule replay verification for Meridian (verify end-to-end traces were reprocessed) (due 2026-12-08).

Risks and mitigation plan:
- Risk: multiple installs using differing on-site network assumptions (MTU, overlay offloads) -> mitigation: shipping a small preflight binary that reports MTU, offload flags, and kernel versions; tie install progress gating to this report.
- Risk: log/telemetry loss during restarts -> mitigation: add buffered handoff (durable cursor) in LogForwarder, plus short-term duplicate-replay option in install-harness.
- Risk: operational complexity for customers new to on-prem GPUs -> mitigation: expand field onboarding checklist to include vault/ntp/nfs id mapping walkthroughs and run a short dry-run before final cutover.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Prioritize MTU preflight and IAM drift checks as blockers for next week (aligned with product to delay non-critical installs).
- Approve a limited scope change to the runbook to include the MTU checker and a one-click preflight report.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Should we require customers to set overlay MTU to 1500 by default for all official installs, or support heterogeneous MTU with additional engineering cost? (Product input needed; action: Maya to align with Product by 2026-12-09).
- What is acceptable telemetry loss window for enterprise customers during planned cutovers? Need SRE + CS guidance to standardize. (Action: Carlos to collect customer SLAs this week).

Meeting artifacts / logs:
- Attachments: staging logs (AtlasPay-cutover-20261207.tgz), Meridian-nfs-trace.log, Quarry-pcap-sample.pcap (uploaded to shared project folder).

Quick wins for next week:
- Add MTU preflight binary to bootstrap and run on all active staging clusters (small PR, target 2026-12-09).
- Add a single-line IAM drift check to the install harness (small PR, target 2026-12-10).

Notes to self:
- Capture a short postmortem template for telemetry gaps (1 page) and attach to PD-723. Keeps recurring incidents consistent.
- Consider a safety toggle in the harness to force-install in degraded mode (only for non-production staging).

Next sync: 2026-12-14, 09:30 PT — focus: progress on MTU + IAM gating, Priya and Jonah to run short demos of their checks.

End of notes.
